# Intake brief — Timed consumable field pickups should use the absorbed-hit model (AH-0MVUVSW4J0009QUW)

**Type:** feature · **Priority:** medium · **Discovered from:** AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW ·
**Blocked by:** AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (dependency edge, parent plan `plan_complete`)

**Producer decisions (2026-10-30):** Q-A1 = **b** (a pickup's charge does **not**
regenerate — one drop buys one event, then the item is inert) · Q-A2 = **a**
(temporary-level TTL reuses today's windows: Shield 15 s, Thorn Field 8 s, Force
Field 8 s) · Q-A3 = **resolved** (AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P is not delivered
separately). See [Decisions](#decisions-producer-2026-10-30).

## Headline

A **field pickup** of Shield, Thorn Field or Force Field should buy **one charge
of one event** (one absorbed hit / one free ram / one reflected bullet) from the
shared consumable charge pool that AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW introduces, instead of
opening a level-resolved **timed window** — and that pickup charge is **not
backed by regeneration**, so a single drop is worth exactly one event. The three
per-kind window axes retire and their level curves re-point at the charge cap /
regeneration interval, so a pickup and a hold-full grant share one model, one
HUD row and one code path, differing only in whether the pool refills.

## Original seed (as filed)

Convert the **timed field pickups** of the budget/consumable power-ups (Shield,
Thorn Field, Force Field) to the same one-event charge model the permanent
consumable pool uses, so a pickup spends a single event (one absorbed hit / one
free ram / one reflected bullet) instead of opening a timed window.

Produced by the producer's answer to **Q2** on AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (*Consumable
upgrades should not be endless*): one charge buys one single event (option b),
and the timed-pickup conversion is deliberately split into this follow-up so that
change lands after the permanent-charge model.

## Problem statement

The run-scoped model now has **two contradictory shapes for the same item**. A
hold-full grant of Shield/Thorn Field/Force Field becomes a **charge pool** (one
event per charge, level-derived cap and regeneration, HUD countdown —
AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW), while a **field pickup** of the same item still opens a
**level-resolved timed window** with its own parallel budget counter and its own
HUD countdown. The player sees "one absorbed hit" from one acquisition path and
"up to 18 seconds of cover" from the other, and the effect path keeps two
mechanisms (window + budget) for what the design calls one thing.

## Users

- **The player** who collects Shield / Thorn Field / Force Field from a drop and
  wants the same legible "one hit, then it comes back" behaviour they get from a
  hold-full grant — not a timer that means a different thing per acquisition
  path.
- **The balance owner**, who needs one bounded unit of value ("one absorbed
  hit") with one level axis pair (cap + regeneration) instead of a window
  duration that silently changes how many events the same pickup buys.
- **The maintainer**, who wants the window machinery deleted rather than
  parallel-cased for three kinds.

**User stories**

- "As a player, when I collect a Shield drop I get **one** absorbed hit — not a
  15-second bubble — and the HUD row tells me when the next absorption is due."
- "As a player, when I collect Thorn Field I get **one** free ram, and when I
  collect Force Field I get **one** reflected bullet; each of them recharges on
  the same rhythm the hold-full version uses."
- "As a balance owner, the three kinds have exactly two level axes each — a
  charge cap and a regeneration interval — and no window duration that changes
  the number of events a pickup is worth."

## Existing state (verified in the repo)

The timed windows for the three kinds are one mechanism with three
instantiations:

- **Shield** — `_applyTimedEffect` opens `shieldDuration` (base 15 s → cap 30 s)
  and sets `_shieldRemaining` to `shieldAbsorptions` (base 1 → cap 3)
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:531-543`); `tryAbsorbShield()` decrements the
  registry-local counter and the last absorption pops the bubble
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:828`).
- **Thorn Field** — `thornsDuration` (8 s → 16 s) window plus `_thornsRemaining`
  from `thornsAbsorbs` (2 → 6), with an **intra-window** refill on
  `thornsRecharge` (12 s → 5 s) that is explicitly gated on the window being
  open (`_advanceThornsRecharge` early-returns via `!this._timed.has('thorns')`,
  `src/powerups/effects.ts:1196-1202`);
  `thornsRechargeRemaining()` returns 0 when there is no active window
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:1177`).
- **Force Field** — `forceFieldDuration` (8 s → 18 s) bubble plus
  `_forceFieldRemaining` from `forceFieldReflects` (3 → 10)
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:588-604`); `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` at
  `src/powerups/effects.ts:922`; the spent-but-dim visual persists after the
  budget is gone (AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z).
- **Catalogue** — the three window axes exist as first-class level variables
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` at `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:219/238/249`;
  specs at `:311`, `:755`, `:892`; stat fields at `:1061`, `:1108`, `:1133`).
- **HUD** — the only consumable regeneration countdown today is Thorn Field's,
  `_powerUpRecharge()` case `'thorns'` → `thornsRechargeRemaining()`
  (`src/ui/HUD.ts:574-580`); Shield and Force Field show no countdown at all.
- **Field-pickup levelling** — a pickup adds one **temporary** level stack and
  the temporary component is cleared by `clearTemporary(id)` when the window
  expires (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:1466-1474`); kinds with no timed
  window keep their temporary stack for the run (Resolved decision 4,
  documented at `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:63-66`). A temporary stack
  occupies a six-slot slot for as long as it lasts
  (`getTempPowerUpIds()`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:1459`).
- **Checkpoints** — permanent grants are replayed through the shared grant seam
  on resume; temporary field-pickup windows are deliberately not persisted and
  never re-open (`docs/Game Design Document.md:1769`).
- **Docs** — the three kinds are documented as *timed* in the GDD player-facing
  table (`docs/Game Design Document.md:965` Shield, `:974` Force Field) and in
  the per-kind level-axis table at `:1196`/`:1205`/`:1209`, with behaviour notes
  at `:1189` (Force Field axes) and `:1190` (Thorn visibility + recharge) and
  the acquisition model at `:1180`.

## Desired change

1. A **field pickup** (`applyCollect(id, false)`) of `shield`, `thorns` or
   `force_field` grants **exactly one charge** into the shared consumable charge
   pool AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW introduces (clamped at the level-resolved cap) and
   **opens no effect window**. The pickup still adds its existing **one
   temporary level stack** (field-pickup levelling is unchanged — the temporary
   stack raises the cap/interval while it lasts and reverts on its own TTL,
   which the sibling item AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A supplies); charges already granted
   are **never clawed back** when that TTL expires (AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC
   resolved decision 2).
2. **A pickup-granted charge does not regenerate (producer decision Q-A1=b).**
   A single drop buys **exactly one event** and the item is **inert afterwards**:
   no charge is banked back for a consumable the player only ever picked up.
   Regeneration is gated on **permanent ownership** — the pool's regenerating
   ceiling for these three kinds is `permanentGrants(id) > 0 ? cap : 0`, so an
   item that was never a hold-full grant never refills on its own. The gate is
   **catalogue data** (a consumable property alongside the parent's `consumable`
   flag), not a per-kind `id === …` special case, and it is **scoped to these
   three kinds**: the shipped regenerating behaviour of Phase Shift / Teleport
   field pickups (AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT) is unchanged.
3. **One charge = one event**, spent through the existing shared consumption
   seams with no new counter: `tryAbsorbShield()` spends one charge (one
   absorbed hit), `tryConsumeThornsRam()` spends one charge (one free ram),
   `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` spends one charge (one reflected bullet).
   The registry-local `_shieldRemaining` / `_thornsRemaining` /
   `_forceFieldRemaining` counters are replaced by pool-derived accessors, so
   there is one source of truth per kind.
4. **Armed means "holds a charge"** — the bubble/aura is drawn while the pool
   has at least one charge and pops when the last charge is spent (the existing
   pop-on-last-absorb path), so the final-second wind-down animation of the
   timed window has no trigger left for Shield and must be either re-pointed at
   the TTL or documented as retired (dead-code decision recorded, not silently
   dropped).
5. **The three window axes retire.** `shieldDuration`, `thornsDuration` and
   `forceFieldDuration` are removed from `PowerUpLevelVariable`,
   `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` and
   `PowerUpLevelStats`; no replacement window axis is introduced. The three
   kinds keep exactly two axes each — the parent's charge cap and regeneration
   interval (`shieldAbsorptions` + new `shieldRecharge`; `thornsAbsorbs` +
   `thornsRecharge`; `forceFieldReflects` + new `forceFieldRecharge`).
6. **The per-kind window TTL resolver must be updated with the retirement.** The
   sibling item AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A resolves a temporary-window TTL per kind
   (timed kinds → their level-resolved effect duration, instant kinds → a
   declared `temporaryWindow` value). After this change these three kinds are
   **instant kinds** for that resolver, so they declare flat `temporaryWindow`
   values (producer decision Q-A2=a) and must not be read through
   `stats.shieldDuration` / `stats.thornsDuration` /
   `stats.forceFieldDuration`.
7. **HUD** — after a pickup these three kinds show the charge count on the
   shared consumable row and **no window countdown**; because a pickup-only
   charge never regenerates, the row shows **no regeneration countdown** either
   (there is nothing to count down), is greyed while owned-and-empty, and
   disappears once the temporary-level TTL expires (the existing field-only
   rule). A **permanently granted** item keeps the parent's full behaviour (live
   `next in Ns` countdown, greyed empty row). The parent's HUD work
   (AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6) owns the rendering; this item owns the assertion that a
   **pickup** lands in the right row state, and removes the Thorn-specific
   `_powerUpRecharge` special case in favour of the shared consumable path.
8. **Parity** — every change lands in the shared core
   (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`,
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) so `PlayScene` and every gym that spawns or
   consumes these kinds inherit it; the duplicate-body guard
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` assertions stay green, and the parity matrix rows for
   these kinds are updated where the retained divergences change.

### Per-kind conversion table

| Kind | Today (field pickup) | After (field pickup) |
|---|---|---|
| Shield | 15 s → 30 s bubble + 1 → 3 absorptions, refreshed on re-collect | 1 charge = **1 absorbed hit**, held until used; **no regeneration** from a pickup; cap `shieldAbsorptions` (1 → 3) and regeneration `shieldRecharge` (45 s → shorter) only once the item is permanently owned; temporary level TTL **15 s** |
| Thorn Field | 8 s → 16 s window + 2 → 6 rams, refilled every 12 s → 5 s *while the window is open* | 1 charge = **1 free ram**, held until used; **no regeneration** from a pickup; cap `thornsAbsorbs` (2 → 6) and regeneration `thornsRecharge` (12 s → 5 s) only once permanently owned; temporary level TTL **8 s** |
| Force Field | 8 s → 18 s bubble + 3 → 10 reflects | 1 charge = **1 reflected bullet**, held until used; **no regeneration** from a pickup; cap `forceFieldReflects` (3 → 10) and regeneration `forceFieldRecharge` (45 s → shorter) only once permanently owned; temporary level TTL **8 s** |

So a drop is worth exactly **one event** (the producer's Q-A1=b scarcity rule), while a
hold-full grant keeps the parent's regenerating pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — A pickup grants exactly one charge and no effect window.** A Shield /
  Thorn Field / Force Field field pickup adds exactly one charge to the shared
  consumable pool, clamped at the level-resolved cap, and opens no effect
  window: no `shieldDuration` / `thornsDuration` / `forceFieldDuration` read
  remains on the path, and the registry's timed map never holds these ids after
  a pickup. It still adds its one temporary level stack. Tests assert pool count
  and clamp per kind, the absence of a window, and that the temporary-stack TTL
  expiry leaves the granted charge intact (no clawback).
- **AC2 — One charge resolves exactly one event and a pickup charge never
  regenerates.** Each spent charge resolves exactly one event (Shield one
  absorbed hit, Thorn Field one free ram, Force Field one reflected bullet); a
  **pickup-only** item then stays empty and **inert** — no regeneration clock
  starts, and a long tick grants nothing (`permanentGrants(id) === 0` ⇒
  regenerating ceiling 0). A **permanently granted** item keeps the parent's
  spend→empty→regenerate→re-use cycle. Both cycles are asserted per kind, in
  `PlayScene`'s shared core and in a gym, with no duplicate counter left behind
  (`_shieldRemaining` / `_thornsRemaining` / `_forceFieldRemaining` removed or
  derived); a regression test pins that Phase Shift / Teleport pickup
  regeneration is unchanged.
- **AC3 — HUD shows the pickup charge with no countdown that cannot happen.**
  After a field pickup the kind's HUD row shows the charge count and **no**
  regeneration or window countdown (a pickup-only charge never regenerates), the
  row is greyed while empty and disappears when the temporary-level TTL expires;
  a permanently granted item's row keeps the parent's live `next in Ns`
  countdown and greyed-empty state. HUD tests cover each state per kind and
  assert that a pickup row never renders a countdown it cannot honour, and the
  Thorn-specific `_powerUpRecharge` case is replaced by the shared consumable
  path.
- **AC4 — The window axes are retired, not orphaned.** `shieldDuration`,
  `thornsDuration` and `forceFieldDuration` are absent from
  `PowerUpLevelVariable`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` and
  `PowerUpLevelStats`, with no remaining reference in `src/` outside tests that
  assert their removal; the change-summary/deferred-axis seam
  (`DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`) stays consistent, and the per-kind
  temporary-window TTL resolver classifies the three kinds as instant kinds with
  the producer-approved flat values — **Shield 15 s, Thorn Field 8 s, Force
  Field 8 s** (coordinated with AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A).
- **AC4b — The no-regeneration gate is catalogue data, not a special case.**
  The "a pickup charge does not regenerate until the item is permanently owned"
  rule is expressed as a consumable property in `src/powerups/types.ts` and read
  by the store/registry; no `id === 'shield' | 'thorns' | 'force_field'` branch
  appears outside the catalogue, and the gate is scoped so Phase Shift / Teleport
  pickup regeneration is unchanged (regression-tested).
- **AC5 — Game and gym behave identically.** All behaviour runs through the
  shared store/registry/`CombatScene` seams; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`
  and the `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` docs assertions pass, and the parity matrix rows
  for the three kinds are updated where a retained divergence changes.
- **AC6 — Checkpoint resume is unchanged and singled out.** A pickup-earned
  charge is not persisted and no window re-opens on resume (existing rule,
  `docs/Game Design Document.md:1769`); a permanent grant still replays through
  the shared grant seam into the same charged state. Regression test asserts
  both, so the conversion cannot quietly start persisting temporary state.
- **AC7 — Documentation updated.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4
  (the player-facing rows at `:965` / `:974`, the acquisition model at `:1180`,
  the behaviour notes at `:1189` / `:1190`, and the per-kind level-axis table at
  `:1196` / `:1205` / `:1209`) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` describe the
  absorbed-hit pickup model, the two axes per kind and the HUD countdown; the
  `src/powerups/effects.ts` and `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` module headers
  no longer describe these kinds as timed.
- **AC8 — Tests and full suite.** New/updated unit tests cover the store grant
  path, the three consumption seams, the retired axes and the HUD row states;
  the full project test suite passes with the change (run through the test
  skill; the dev-push gate enforces it).

## Constraints

- **Must land after AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW.** The shared charge pool, the
  charge/regeneration accessors and the HUD row work are that item's; this item
  consumes them and must not implement a parallel pool.
- **No parallel implementation.** One pool, one grant path, one spend path per
  kind — the shared store/registry seams, never a per-scene copy.
- **No rebalance beyond the model.** Do not change the shipped caps
  (`shieldAbsorptions` 1 → 3, `thornsAbsorbs` 2 → 6, `forceFieldReflects`
  3 → 10) or the parent's regeneration curves; the only value changes are the
  retired window axes and the producer-approved temporary-level TTLs (Shield
  15 s, Thorn Field 8 s, Force Field 8 s).
- **Scarcity rule (Q-A1=b).** A pickup-granted charge is worth **one event** and
  never refills unless the item is permanently owned; do not soften this into a
  token regeneration "just for pickups", and do not extend the rule to Phase
  Shift / Teleport, whose shipped pickup regeneration (AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT) is
  unchanged.
- **No clawback.** Charges already granted survive a temporary-level TTL
  expiry (AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC resolved decision 2).
- **Coordinate with in-flight work on the same surface:**
  - AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P (*Permanent Force Field should regenerate its reflect
    budget*, blocked/intake_complete) — **producer decision Q-A3: resolved, do
    not deliver it separately.** Its remaining scope (a `forceFieldRecharge`
    axis + dim-to-bright refill + countdown) is **subsumed** by the parent for
    permanents and by this item for pickups, so it has been **re-scoped** (not
    deleted, so the requirement cannot be lost if the parent changes) and given
    a blocking dependency edge to this item so its conflicting axis cannot land
    first. It is to be **closed** once this item and the parent ship.
  - AH-0MVUGI448000GNMJ (*F3: Instant-kind temporary windows and revert at
    expiry*) — after this change these three kinds are instant kinds for that
    item's window treatment; this item's "no effect window" and F3's
    "temporary-level TTL window" are different windows and must not be
    conflated (the effect is charge-bounded; the level has a TTL).
  - AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A (*F2: Per-upgrade temporary-window TTL in the
    catalogue*) — reads `stats.shieldDuration` / `forceFieldDuration` for timed
    kinds, so its resolver must reclassify these three (AC4).
  - AH-0MVUGI4WG008HU3M (*F5: Consumables, slots and HUD follow expiry*) — its
    AC5/AC6 premises (window countdown, slot released at window expiry) change
    for these kinds; re-read it before landing.
- **Out of scope.** Timed non-consumable kinds (Speed Boost, Frenzy, Chrono,
  Salvage, Magnet/Mineral Scoop), periodic rewards (Bomb, Smart Bomb, Orbital
  Strike) and Mystery UFO's own pickup/vacuum behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `_applyTimedEffect` cases `shield` / `thorns` /
  `force_field` become charge grants with no window; `_shieldRemaining`,
  `_thornsRemaining`, `_forceFieldRemaining` deleted or derived from the pool;
  `tryAbsorbShield` / `tryConsumeThornsRam` / `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect`
  spend through the shared pool; `thornsRechargeRemaining()` and
  `_advanceThornsRecharge` lose their "window is open" gating; module header
  rewritten.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — remove `shieldDuration`, `thornsDuration`,
  `forceFieldDuration` from the variable union, the ordered list, the specs and
  the stats type; keep the two axes per kind; update the module header and the
  temporary/permanent documentation block.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — consumable descriptions/catalogue copy for the three
  kinds, the parent's `consumable` flag, and the new
  **no-regeneration-from-pickups** property (the Q-A1=b gate) plus the
  temporary-level TTL values (15 s / 8 s / 8 s); coordinated with
  AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW and AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — drop the Thorn-specific `_powerUpRecharge` case for the
  shared consumable countdown path; assert the pickup row state.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — consumption call sites stay, but the
  armed/empty conditions read the pool (`isForceFieldActive`, thorns aura
  visibility) rather than a live window.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — bubble/aura arming follows
  "pool holds a charge"; the Shield final-second wind-down has no trigger left
  (re-point or document).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/__tests__/temporaryRevert.test.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — the window assertions per kind
  become charge assertion cycles.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (`:965`, `:974`, `:1180`, `:1189`,
  `:1190`, `:1196`, `:1205`, `:1209`) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Related work

- **Predecessor/blocker:** AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW — *Consumable upgrades should not
  be endless* (open, `plan_complete`). Supplies the shared charge pool (F2
  AH-0MVUXH0T0001N3C2), the one-event consumption/regeneration accessors (F3
  AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3), the HUD countdown (F4 AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6) and the docs
  pass (F7 AH-0MVUXH4PX0009KZR).
- **Overlap to resolve:** AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P — *Permanent Force Field should
  regenerate its reflect budget* (blocked, `intake_complete`). Same surface; its
  scope is subsumed by the parent (permanents) and this item (pickups).
- **Coordination:** AH-0MVUGI448000GNMJ (*F3: Instant-kind temporary windows and
  revert at expiry*), AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A (*F2: Per-upgrade temporary-window
  TTL*), AH-0MVUGI4WG008HU3M (*F5: Consumables, slots and HUD follow expiry*).
- **Precedent:** AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT (*Per-charge recharge engine*, completed),
  AH-0MV82I8IL0012RXY (*Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence*,
  completed), AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T (*What does Field of Thorns do?*, completed —
  the Thorn aura + `next in Ns` countdown), AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (*temporary
  rather than permanent pickups*, completed), AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z (spent-dim
  bubble persistence).
- **Filed follow-up coverage:** the parent's AC8 already files this item
  (`discovered-from:AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW`, blocked by it), so intake is a
  definition pass, not a creation pass.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Balance — the drop is now much weaker (high, resolution safety-critical).**
  Under Q-A1=b a Force Field drop buys **one** reflection (today: 3–10 inside
  8–18 s) and a Thorn Field drop buys **one** ram (today: 2–6 inside 8–16 s).
  This is the producer's chosen scarcity, but it is a visible nerf to two
  popular drops and could make them read as broken in play. Mitigations: the
  granted charge **persists until used** (no window to waste), the cap axes are
  unchanged, and the change should be watched with the existing balance/eval
  harness; if it proves too weak the fix is a catalogue/level change, not a
  code change.
- **Consumable-consistency (medium).** After this change Shield / Thorn Field /
  Force Field pickups do **not** regenerate while Phase Shift / Teleport pickups
  do. That asymmetry is deliberate (Q-A1=b, scoped to the three converted
  kinds) but is exactly the sort of split that gets "normalised" by a later
  refactor, so AC4b/AC2 pin it with regression tests and the docs state the
  reason.
- **Dead-code/coupling (medium).** Retiring three catalogue axes removes the
  read path another in-flight item's TTL resolver leans on
  (AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A) and a Shield wind-down animation whose trigger
  disappears. Both must be handled explicitly (AC4, Desired change 4), not left
  as broken references.
- **HUD/slot semantics (medium).** These kinds leave the "timed window" class, so
  the F5 (AH-0MVUGI4WG008HU3M) premises around row countdown and slot release at
  window expiry no longer hold; the temporary *level* now expires on its own TTL
  while the charge persists — a combination no existing test covers today.
- **Test churn (medium).** `shieldDuration` / `thornsDuration` /
  `forceFieldDuration` appear across `effects.test.ts`,
  `powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `temporaryRevert.test.ts` and `HUD.test.ts`; the
  window assertions must be rewritten as charge-cycle assertions rather than
  deleted, or the coverage for these kinds silently drops.
- **Scope creep (low).** The conversion invites "why not Frenzy/Chrono/Salvage
  too?" and "why doesn't my pickup refill?" — both deliberately out of scope
  (recorded as linked work, not expanded here).
- **Assumption A1.** A field pickup of these kinds still adds **one temporary
  level stack** (keeping today's levelling), so repeated pickups raise the cap
  for the run; the level TTL is the producer-approved flat value from the
  sibling item AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A, not a level curve (the duration axes that
  used to grow it are retired).
- **Assumption A2.** "Opens no timed window" refers to the **effect** window
  (the 8–18 s bubble/aura), not the temporary-*level* TTL; the two are distinct
  concepts and both can be true at once.
- **Assumption A3.** The HUD needs no new widget — the parent's `next in Ns`
  formatter and greyed-empty-row rules cover these kinds; this item only proves
  the pickup path reaches that state (and renders no countdown when nothing
  regenerates).
- **Assumption A6.** The Q-A1=b gate means "regenerating ceiling = cap when
  permanently owned, 0 otherwise" — a single derived number, not a second
  charge counter, and it is scoped to the three converted kinds so Phase
  Shift / Teleport pickup regeneration is untouched.
- **Assumption A7.** Because the duration axes retire, the temporary-level TTL
  is **flat** (no longer level-derived); a levelled item's temporary stack no
  longer lasts longer than a level-0 one. Recorded as an intentional
  consequence of Q-A2=a (`a` was chosen to preserve today's *level-0* window
  length).

## Goal

**User story:** as an engineer running the full suite alongside other agent sessions, I want the gym↔game spawn-parity cases to have a timeout that reflects their real cost, so a busy host produces a green run instead of a spurious critical test-failure item.

## Background

Producer decision (2026-10-31, during the audit of AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC): **yes**, add an explicit per-case timeout.

Evidence: two red runs failed *different* cases just over vitest's 5 s default — `5050 ms` (Robotron horde) at HEAD `d828dab45` and `5162 ms` (Pac-Man ghost group) at HEAD `22ed236b4` — while a full-scope rerun at `22ed236b4` was green (380 files / 8592 tests passed, 3 expected fail). Each case boots two full Phaser scenes and steps 1600 frames (`src/scenes/gym/spawnParity.test.ts:1031` and the surrounding release loop), so the default timeout is below the worst-case cost under contention.

## Suggested approach

- Give every case in the `cases` table an explicit per-case timeout (e.g. `it(name, fn, 30_000)`), or wrap the shared body in a helper that supplies it — one place, not per case.
- Consider the same treatment for the sibling scene-parity suites if they show the same signature (`levelParity.test.ts`, `GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`); record any deliberate choice not to.
- Do not weaken assertions: this is a timeout bound only, no behavioural change.

- AC1 — Every case in `src/scenes/gym/spawnParity.test.ts` runs with an explicit timeout comfortably above its worst-case cost (>= 20 s), applied in one shared place rather than per case.
- AC2 — No assertion is removed, relaxed or skipped; the suite's 10 cases and their parity claims are unchanged.
- AC3 — Full suite green through the test skill (`run_tests.py`) with the timeout in place, run recorded in a comment.
- AC4 — The change is test-only; no production code is touched.

## Constraints

- Tests only — no production behaviour change.

- **Q1 — scope of AC1: "every case" means all 10 cases.** AC1 stands as written: one shared mechanism must give the explicit timeout to all 10 test cases in `src/scenes/gym/spawnParity.test.ts` — the 5 singleton `it()` sites (orbital spawn transit, launched-wave fire cadence, launched march block, GymBotTuning inheritance, Diver re-anchor) **and** the 5 parametrised D3 cases from the `cases` table. The timeout applied so far covers only the D3 loop, so the implementation must be extended before commit: use a single file-level mechanism (e.g. `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 30_000 })` in the test file, or one shared `itParity()` wrapper that every `it` site calls) rather than repeating a literal per case.

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** chore (process/tooling; no gameplay behaviour change) ·
**Status:** CONFIRMED — producer answered Q1 (a), Q2 "as recommended" (= d), Q3 (a) on 2026-11-01.

**Decision (producer, 2026-11-01):** *verify-and-narrow*. The filed premise no
longer reproduces against the installed skills; this item now proves the scoped
gate works in a real `implement.py finish`, documents the node/vitest selection
order, and records the wall-clock measurement. Residual selector gaps are
**out of scope here** and filed on framework item **SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO**
(comment `SA-C0MVXW2CB8003BXPJ`); no agent-infrastructure edits from this repo.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` is documented to validate **changed scope only** for fast
iteration, but at filing time every finish gate in this repository logged
`changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope` and then ran
the full Vitest suite (≈ 346–409 s loaded, plus host-wide test-slot queueing).

Read-only verification during intake shows the **skill-level fix landed after
this item was filed** and the fallback no longer reproduces: the installed
selector maps vitest `.test.ts`/`.spec.ts` files and picks a subset for every one
of the last 25 commits. What has *not* happened is proof in a real gate (no
finish gate has run since the install), plus documentation and a measurement.
This item delivers exactly that proof.

## Users (user stories)

- *As an implementing agent*, I want `implement.py finish` on a single-file
  change to run only the affected tests, so the build → test → commit loop
  completes in minutes rather than queueing 1–2 h for a full-suite slot.
- *As a producer*, I want the changed-scope gate to still fail on a
  deliberately broken affected test, and the full suite to remain the
  `dev`-push gate, so speed never weakens correctness.
- *As a maintainer of this repo*, I want the node/vitest selection order
  documented so the behaviour is predictable and diagnosable.

## Existing state (verified 2026-11-01, read-only)

The filed log line —

```
WARNING: Implement run_tests: changed-scope selection unavailable in <worktree>
(no dev baseline, no changed tests, custom suiteCommands, or node-only selection)
```

— is the *old* generic message. All five matching logs under `.worklog/tmp/`
(2026-10-31 05:50 → 22:35) contain exactly that text. The installed message is
now specific:
`changed-scope selection unavailable in <path> (<specific reason>)`.

  `_run_changed_scope_selection` (shared `run_tests.changed_scope_selection`)
  → full suite. The pytest-only `_run_changed_scope_pytest` path described in
  the original root cause is no longer the general path.
- `run_tests.py` now (a) recognises `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` / `.js` / `.tsx`
  test files in `map_changed_to_tests`, (b) emits
  `node_modules/.bin/vitest run <files>` when the repo uses Vitest, and
  (c) no longer lets `suiteCommands` disable selection (it describes the full
  suite only). Docstrings cite **SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO**; the fix was committed
  2026-10-30 20:13 and installed here 2026-10-31 23:59 (`run_tests.py`) /
  2026-11-01 00:45 (`implement.py`) — **after** this item was filed (15:25 on
  2026-10-31) and after every observed fallback log.

- `run_tests.changed_scope_selection(<repo>)` over the changed file set of each

WARNING: Implement run_tests: changed-scope selection unavailable in <worktree> (no dev baseline, no changed tests, custom suiteCommands, or node-only selection) — falling back to full scope.
```

2. `_run_changed_scope_pytest` — pytest-specific, returns None for a Vitest project;
3. fallback: full suite.

- **B. Skill-level:** add a Vitest (node) changed-file → test-file selector alongside the pytest one so step 2 works for node projects (affects every node repo, not just this one).

Record the chosen option and measure: before/after wall-clock time of `implement.py finish` on a single-file change, and that the full suite still runs at the dev-push pre-push hook (unchanged).

### Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A single-file change in this repository makes `implement.py finish` run a **subset** of the suite; the fallback warning is gone from the finish log.
- **AC2:** The gate output names the selected group/tests, and a deliberately failing affected test still fails the gate.
- **AC3:** Behaviour for projects without group configuration is unchanged (existing `_run_resolved_suite` / `run_tests` tests pass).
- **AC4:** Docs updated (`docs/dev/` implement/test-skill reference) describing the selection order for node projects.

# [test-failure] compile-promo.e2e: validation CLI exits 1 after a successful compile

## Problem statement

The gated real-ffmpeg end-to-end test `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts` fails with
`AssertionError: expected 1 to be +0` (test file line 153), even though every deliverable
encodes successfully with real ffmpeg. The compile's **editorial package-size gate**
(`report.targets`, added after the e2e test was written) rejects the test's deliberately
short synthetic fixture: a ~4.7 s promo against a 45–60 s floor, a ~4.8 s showreel against
a > 2 min floor and 2 highlight clips against a 5-clip target. The per-deliverable
validation and the pace gate pass; the failure is a sizing verdict, not a broken encode.

The test's current assertions (`expect(result.code).toBe(0)`, `toContain('all validated OK')`)
therefore encode a contract the fixture can never satisfy, so the gated `e2e` signal is
permanently red and can no longer flag real encoder regressions.

## Users

- **Agent implementer** running `/skill:test --type e2e` or the release verification:
  needs the e2e suite green so a red `e2e` run means a genuine real-encoder/validation
  regression, not a known-bad editorial sizing assertion.
- **Producer / reviewer** auditing the release: needs the e2e failure (when it happens) to
  name the offending deliverable/target instead of only `expected 1 to be +0`.
- **Maintainer of the promo compiler** changing `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`: needs the
  gated smoke test to keep proving "a real ffmpeg accepts the production command line and
  produces a probeable 960×540 VP9+Opus WebM", without pretending to prove editorial sizing.

Example user story:

> As an agent running the gated e2e suite, I want `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts` to
> assert exactly the contract its synthetic fixture can prove (encodability,
> per-deliverable validation, pace, and the *expected* editorial-size rejection for a
> deliberately short package), so that a green run is meaningful and a red run names the
> deliverable that drifted.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root cause evidenced from the validator's own output.** The failing invocation's
   stdout/report is captured in a work-item comment and shows: all four deliverables
   `ok` (promo, showreel, highlight-01, highlight-02), `pace OK`, and `targets FAIL`
   with the issues naming the short promo, the short showreel and the missing highlight
   clips. If the observed cause differs, the brief's diagnosis is corrected in the same
   comment before implementing.
2. **The e2e test asserts the contract the fixture can prove.** After the fix, the test
   asserts per-deliverable validation success (vp9 960×540, opus audio, brightness above
   the calibrated floor, expected duration band), `report.pace.ok === true`, and the
   editorial size outcome — either explicitly excluded by a documented,
   test-only mechanism **or** asserted as the expected rejection with its target-specific
   issues. No blanket relaxation of the exit code (e.g. bare `expect([0,1]).toContain(...)`).
3. **Failures are actionable.** Any real validation drift makes the assertion message name
   the offending deliverable and/or target issues (e.g. include
   `result.stdout` / `result.compileResult.report.errors` in the assertion message), so a
   future failure is never just "expected 1 to be 0".
4. **Gated run passes on an ffmpeg host.** `python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --type e2e`
   passes for `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts` on a host with `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` on
   `PATH`, and still `skipIf`s cleanly when they are absent. The `e2e` project also holds
   `scripts/capture-seekable.e2e.test.ts` and `scripts/tune-verify.e2e.test.ts`, so when those
   are unrelated to this change, record both the file-scoped run for this test and the
   full-project result rather than letting another member's state stand in for this one.
5. **No weakened production gate and no slower fixture.** `EDITORIAL_CONFIG.targets`
   (promo 45–60 s, showreel > 2 min, 5 highlights) and `EDITORIAL_CONFIG.paceBand` keep
   their current values, and `npm run compile:promo` on a genuinely short capture pool
   still exits non-zero. The e2e fixture durations are not lengthened (no new
   ~140 s+ encode cost).
6. **Docs and help text updated.** Whatever precondition/flag is chosen is documented in
   `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` (§7.6, next to the pace band and the deliverable-size
   verification paragraphs that close it) and, if a
   CLI flag is introduced, in `USAGE_TEXT`; affected code comments are updated so the
   e2e's scope is explicit where the test is defined.
7. **Regression tests for any production change.** If `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` gains a
   flag/parameter, `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` covers argument parsing, the summary
   text and the gate-skipping behaviour hermetically (no real ffmpeg).
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (`/skill:test --type full`), and
   all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
   README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **The editorial targets are product requirements, not test knobs** — 45–60 s promo,
  > 2 min showreel and 5 highlight clips come from AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4 / epic AC1 and must
  not be lowered to make the test green.
- **The e2e must stay cheap.** It is the single most expensive `scripts/` test (~140 s floor,
  measured in AH-0MVF6VQ7G005ALXZ) and was deliberately moved out of the audit-accepted
  default suite by AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP. Do not grow the fixture to satisfy the size gate.
- **Real-encoder coverage must not be lost.** The test's unique value is "a real ffmpeg
  accepts the production command line and the output probes as VP9 960×540 + Opus with
  non-trivial brightness"; every assertion kept must still exercise that path.
- **No production behaviour change for real captures** unless it is the explicit,
  documented opt-out described above; `npm run compile:promo` verdicts on real footage must
  be unchanged.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` / gym↔game parity is out of scope (different subsystem).

## Existing state

- `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts` (last changed in `ac1aa2072`, AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP) builds
  two 3.2 s / 2.6 s synthetic `testsrc2` sources (320×180@30, `-cpu-used 8`) with one action
  peak each, then calls `compilePromoMain(['--compile', '--runs', ..., '--out', planPath,
  '--out-dir', outDir])` and asserts `code === 0` plus `stdout` contains `all validated OK`.
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` `compileDeliverables()` now fails the compile on two gates
  beyond per-deliverable validation: `assessPace()` (opening/overall non-black ≥ 90 %,
  mean recorded intensity ≥ 0.3) and `assessTargets()` (promo 45–60 s, showreel ≥ 120 s,
  ≥ 5 highlight clips). `assessTargets()` entered the compile flow in `bb8cc6faa`
  (AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4) — **after** the e2e test's last change — so the e2e has been red
  since then, deterministically, whenever ffmpeg is present.
- With the synthetic fixture, `deliverables` = promo + showreel + 2 highlights
  (highlight-01, highlight-02) spanning ~4.7 s and ~4.8 s, so `assessTargets()` reports
  "promo is 4.7s, below the 45.0s target", "showreel is 4.8s, below the 120.0s target" and
  "only 2 highlight clip(s) produced, target 5"; `formatCompileSummary()` prints
  `targets FAIL` and `Validation report: ...`, and `compilePromoMain()` returns code 1.
- Unaffected by this: the same gates are covered hermetically in `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`
  (`assessPace`, `assessTargets`, injected-subprocess orchestration) and documented in
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.6 (pace band plus the deliverable-size verification
  paragraphs that close it).

## Desired change

Make the gated e2e assert what its synthetic fixture can actually prove, and make the
editorial-size outcome explicit rather than an accidental exit-code mismatch:

- **Preferred approach (documented precondition, no production behaviour change):** keep
  the strict `code`-independent assertions on the report — every deliverable `ok`, correct
  codec/resolution/audio/brightness/duration, `pace.ok === true` — and assert the
  **expected** `targets.ok === false` with target-specific issues that explain the short
  synthetic package (promo/showreel below target, fewer than 5 highlights). Include the
  stdout/report errors in assertion messages so real drift is named. Document in
  `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` and a comment at the top of the test that synthetic
  fixtures cannot satisfy the editorial size targets, and that sizing is verified by the
  unit suites + `npm run compile:promo` on real captures.
- **Alternative (explicit, documented opt-out):** add a narrowly-scoped, documented CLI
  switch (e.g. `--smoke` / `--skip-size-gates`) that disables only the editorial size gate
  (never per-deliverable validation, never the pace gate), records in the report that the
  gate was skipped (so the AC stays auditable), is covered hermetically in
  `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` and documented in `USAGE_TEXT` + docs. The e2e then keeps
  `code === 0` / `all validated OK` semantics.

Either way the test must remain a real-encoder test (no injected ffmpeg) and must not
change the fixture durations.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts` — primary fix: assert `report.pace`/`report.targets`/
  deliverable verdicts (or the smoke opt-out) and put the report/stdout issues into
  assertion messages.
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — only if the alternative opt-out is chosen: `USAGE_TEXT`,
  `parseCompileArgs()`, `compileDeliverables()` gate handling, `compilePromoMain()` wiring,
  `formatCompileSummary()` reporting of the skipped gate.
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — hermetic coverage for any new flag/parse/summary
  behaviour and for the gate-skip reporting.
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` (§7.6 pace reference band, whose closing paragraphs are the
  deliverable-size verification — there is no §7.7) — record the synthetic-fixture
  precondition or the smoke switch.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` — only if the e2e invocation/flags documented there change
  (it already documents `npm run test:e2e` and `--type e2e`).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — `### Validation` lists the gates a compiled package must
  pass and the test-file table row describes this e2e's scope; both are guarded by
  `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts` (`exits non-zero`, `target sizing`, `§7.6`), so any doc
  wording added here must keep those assertions true.
- `README.md` — the `e2e` project bullet states that `e2e` "only proves a real encoder accepts
  the command line and produces probe-able output"; update it if the asserted contract changes
  (AC8).
- `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts` — update assertions if `USAGE_TEXT` or documented commands
  change.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ** — ffmpeg compile driver and output validation (origin of the e2e
  smoke test and the per-deliverable validator).
- **AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4** (`bb8cc6faa`) — added the runtime pace/size verification that now
  rejects the e2e fixture; its ACs own the 45–60 s / > 2 min / 5-clip targets.
- **AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP** (`ac1aa2072`) — producer decision gating this test as the `e2e`
  type; constrains any change that would make the e2e slower or weaker.
- **AH-0MVF6VQ7G005ALXZ** — bounded-fixture measurements (~140 s floor) that rule out
  lengthening the fixture.
- **AH-0MVDV4RJ300459ZF** — `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` as the single source of truth for targets,
  pace band and cut cadence.
- **AH-0MVSE1PG7006XBZ9** — the e2e run in which this failure was observed
  (`discovered-from`), and its parent epic AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B (out of scope here).
- Rather than blocking: this failure is independent of the tune-loop safety epic; it only
  affects the gated `e2e` signal.

Docs: `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.6 (pace band + deliverable-size verification),
`docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (e2e type), `README.md` (test types table),
`src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts` (documentation contract tests).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: masking real validation regressions** if the exit code is relaxed. Mitigation:
  keep per-deliverable and pace assertions strict and assert the size-gate outcome
  explicitly (AC2/AC3).
- **Risk: scope creep into editing the product targets.** Explicitly out of scope
  (Constraints); record any further opportunity as a separate work item.
- **Risk: fixture growth for coverage's sake.** Rejected by AH-0MVF6VQ7G005ALXZ measurements
  and AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP's decision; AC5 pins this.
- **Risk: a new CLI flag becomes de-facto production surface** (someone runs
  `--skip-size-gates` for a real release). Mitigation if the alternative is chosen: name it
  for smoke use, document it as test-only in `USAGE_TEXT`, and record the skip in the report.
- **Assumption (to verify first, AC1):** the failure is deterministic under real ffmpeg
  because of the fixture's short durations, not host-specific encoding drift. The reported
  run showed all four deliverables `ok` with real ffmpeg at
  `/home/rgardler/.local/bin/ffmpeg`, which is consistent with a size-gate verdict.
- **Assumption:** no other consumer depends on `compilePromoMain()` returning `0` for an
  undersized synthetic package.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the failing contract is determinable from the repository
(the e2e fixture's 3.2 s/2.6 s sources versus `EDITORIAL_CONFIG.targets`), and the seed item
already bounds the acceptable outcomes ("either the validator's expectations match what the
compiler produces on this host, or the test documents the environmental precondition").

- Q: "Which fix direction should the implementer take — assert the expected size-gate rejection
  with a documented precondition, or add a test-only gate opt-out?" — **Not blocking**: the
  seed item permits either. **Recommended:** documented precondition with the rejection
  asserted explicitly (no production behaviour change); it keeps the gate exercised and adds
  no test-only CLI surface. Answer recorded as an implementation choice for the implement
  stage, to be confirmed by the evidenced output in AC1.

AssertionError: expected 43.75 to be greater than or equal to 44.50000000000001
 ❯ expectCadenceAround src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts:152:20
 150| function expectCadenceAround(scene: GymLevel, expected: number) {
 152|   expect(measured).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(expected - 0.5);
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout <commit-hash>` (the latest `dev` is the reference).
2. Run the failing test **through the test-skill runner** (this repo is TypeScript/Vitest — the `pytest` command in the triage template above is wrong and must not be used): `python3 $(skill_path test)/scripts/run_tests.py --scope changed --json`, or `--scope full` before `in_review`.

4. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts > GymBotTuning — inherits level-scaled counts and cadence (AH-0MVLJF6ZD00164MG) > AC2 — a level-10 probe runs the shared scaled counts and lengthened cadence (no fork)` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
4. The test is no longer shard/concurrency dependent: repeated runs pass with
   `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2` (the configuration under which
   it failed twice on 2026-10-31), as well as at the default concurrency.
5. The fix does not weaken the parity assertion: the test still fails if the
   gym stops applying the shared level scaling (level-10 ×2 enemy counts and
   the ×3.6 lengthened supply cadence).

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Clarification (plan review, 2026-11-01)

The failure is **concurrency/sharding dependent**, not a stable `dev`
regression. Recorded evidence (see comments):

- `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2`: full suite failed twice in a
  row on this exact assertion (`expected 43.75 to be >= 44.5`; the level-10
  cadence should be 45.0 ± 0.5).
- Default concurrency (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`): the same
  tree passed the full suite.

### Suspected mechanism

The cadence is derived as
`expectedCadenceInterval(level) = DEFAULT_RULES.powerUpSpawnInterval /
dropChanceRatio(level, DEFAULT_RULES)` and the scene resolves the same formula
from `loadRules()` (`GymLevel._resolveSupplyInterval`). The measured 43.75 s
corresponds to a drop-chance ratio of ~0.2857 instead of 0.2778 — i.e. a rules
value (`powerUpSpawnInterval`, `powerUpDropChanceAtLevel1` or
`powerUpDropChanceAtMaxLevel`) leaked from a neighbouring test in the same
worker. `GymBotTuning`'s `beforeEach` calls `resetBotTuningStore()` and clears
`localStorage` but does not reset the rules/config store state that
`loadRules()` reads, so a sibling test's persisted/tuned rules can survive into
this case.

### Suggested fix direction

- Assert the cadence against the **cadence the scene itself resolved** (or the
  same `loadRules()` source the scene used) instead of the test's module-level
  `DEFAULT_RULES`; and/or
- reset the shipped rules/config store in `beforeEach`/`afterEach` (the pattern
  the other gym parity tests use) so no neighbouring test's values leak in.
- Keep the level-10 assertion meaningful: the test must still fail if the gym
  stops applying the shared level scaling (×2 counts, ×3.6 cadence). Do not
  "fix" this by loosening the ±0.5 s tolerance or dropping the assertion.

### Out of scope

- Reworking the level-scaling curve or the shipped cadence values.
- Any change to `PlayScene` or the formation gyms' documented flat cadence.

**Key Files:**

- src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts
- src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts
- src/core/levelScaling.ts
- src/core/rules.ts
- src/core/configStore.ts
- src/core/botTuningStore.ts

- No clarifying questions were required. The work item's evidence plus the
  producer comments (AH-C0MVWRIJ5N009DE5O) were sufficient to scope a single
  test-isolation fix; the plan pre-check returned `decision: "skip"` (effort
  Extra Small, risk Low), so planning was auto-completed after the six review
  stages rather than decomposed into child items.
- OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, for the implementer): confirm the exact leaking
  rules field by running the full suite at the raised concurrency before and
  after the reset change; record the finding in a comment. This does not block
  starting the fix.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-01 (plan skill, downtime dispatch): auto-completed planning after the
  six review stages (pre-check `skip` — Extra Small / Low). Replaced the
  incorrect `pytest` reproduction command with the test-skill runner, added the
  concurrency-dependent failure context, suspected mechanism, suggested fix
  direction, out-of-scope list and a validated **Key Files** section; added

# Intake brief — Flaky unseeded PlayScene.test.ts integration assertions (boss phase advance, level-advance alive count)

**Headline:** Make the `PlayScene` integration boots reproducible (explicit run seed plus no live animation frame while a test asserts), so the boss-phase-advance and level-advance alive-count assertions only go red on a real regression.

## Problem statement

Two exact-count assertions in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load — one run each on two consecutive full-suite runs at dev tip `18f51aca9` — even though both passed in the immediately preceding gates on the same tree. A red full-suite gate therefore no longer means a real regression: it blocks `dev` pushes and triggers `test-failure` triage.

## Users

- **AI agents and producers running the full-suite gate** — a flaky red gate blocks every `dev` push and burns a retry cycle plus a triage item.
- **Maintainers of `PlayScene`, wave spawning and the boss encounter** — they need these two assertions to keep proving the real contract (phase advances exactly once per hit pool; a fresh wave starts fully spawned).

Example user stories:

- *As an agent whose `implement.py finish` gate runs the full suite, I want `PlayScene.test.ts` to be reproducible, so an unrelated docs-only change is never blocked by a random red run.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the boss-phase and wave-alive assertions to stay exact (not weakened to "at least one"), so a genuine double-advance or a lost spawn is still caught.*

## Existing state (evidence)

- Failure 1 (run A): `PlayScene — boss encounter (AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ) > AC2 — the 4-phase health bar depletes and advances the phase on hits` — `AssertionError: expected 3 to be 2` at `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:2028` (`boss.getPhaseNumber()` after `damageBossPhase(scene, boss)`).
- Failure 2 (run B): `PlayScene — playable run (AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3) > AC5 — clearing a level advances to the next level automatically` — `AssertionError: expected 8 to be 9` at `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:1107` (`scene.getAliveCount()` vs `wm.waveEnemyCount()`).
- Both passed in the child-finish gates for AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD and AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV on the same tree, so they are intermittent rather than deterministic.
- `bootPlay()` (`PlayScene.test.ts:654`) and `bootPlayAtBoss()` (`:669`) inject no run seed **and** leave the harness's resumed live `requestAnimationFrame` loop running. `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` (`:684`) does both: it calls `result.scene.setRng(FIXED_RNG)` and `result.booted.game.loop.stop()`.
- `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:5908`) draws `randomSeed()` (backed by `Math.random()`) when nothing is injected, and `setRunSeed()` (`:5798`) is only read at the next `create()`. `bootSceneWithLevels()` (`:547`) calls `scene.scene.restart()` then `await advanceGame(...)`, so a seed must be injected *before* that restart (the pattern already used by `bootWithHordeWave()` at `:6261`).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` boots deterministically with fixed deltas but **resumes** the live loop afterwards, so real frames with wall-clock deltas can still run at any `await` boundary.
- `getAliveCount()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:5241`) counts spawned-and-alive entities, so a wave whose later groups are released on the wave timer (rather than by `finishSpawnAnimations()`) can legitimately be one short at the instant the test asserts.
- Precedent in this same file: AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R (asteroid heading) and AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU (Robotron horde kill) both required a **reproduced seed** before a fix was accepted; a green re-run was explicitly rejected as evidence.

## Candidate mechanisms (to confirm during implementation)

1. **Unseeded run seed** — drop rolls, power-up rolls, enemy behaviour and spawn planning differ per run, so an exact phase index / alive count can land one out.
2. **Resumed live rAF loop** — a real frame with a large wall-clock delta can advance wave timers, spawn release and collisions between the harness's `await` points on a loaded host. Seeding alone cannot fix this.
3. **Spawn-window timing** — `finishSpawnAnimations()` completes the wormhole transit of *already released* entities; a group still pending on the wave timer is not counted yet, which matches the observed 8-vs-9 shortfall.

## Desired change

Give every `PlayScene` boot helper in the integration file a deterministic, reproducible starting state (explicit run seed injected before `create()`/`restart`, and no live animation frame while the test drives and asserts), after reproducing each named failure on pre-fix code with a recorded seed. Keep the two assertions exact where determinism makes them exact; where a test must tolerate in-flight state, assert the invariant instead, with a comment saying why.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reproduction recorded before the fix:** a specific run seed is found that makes *each* of the two named assertions fail on pre-fix code, and is recorded in a work-item comment (command + seed + observed failure). A green re-run on its own is not accepted as evidence.
2. **Deterministic boots:** every `boot*` helper in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` that boots a `PlayScene` injects an explicit deterministic run seed before `create()`/`restart` (through one shared helper, mirroring `bootPlayWithAsteroid()`'s `FIXED_RNG` and `bootWithHordeWave()`'s `setRunSeed`), so repeated runs of any suite in the file observe identical initial state.
3. **No live frame during assertions (producer-confirmed as part of the required deterministic boot, not an optional extra):** `bootPlay()` and `bootPlayAtBoss()` — and any other helper whose suite asserts exact counts — stop the resumed live rAF loop for the duration of the test, mirroring `bootPlayWithAsteroid()`, so no wall-clock frame can advance state between `await` points.
4. **Both named assertions pass deterministically:** three consecutive `/skill:test --scope changed` runs that include `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, with no seed injected by the environment, plus the `dev`-push full-suite gate. (Producer-confirmed verification channel; ad-hoc `vitest` and single-file runs remain out of scope.)
5. **Invariants where in-flight state is legitimate:** any test that must tolerate in-flight bullets or spawn-animation lag asserts the invariant instead of an exact instantaneous count (e.g. phase index monotonicity, or alive count after the wave's spawn window is fully released), with a comment explaining why.
6. **Test-only change:** no behaviour change in `src/` production code; only existing seams are used (`setRunSeed`, `setRng`, `game.loop.stop()`).
7. **Documentation updated:** the in-file comments explain the deterministic boot and the seed policy; any related docs are updated to reflect the changes.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-execution policy:** agent-initiated runs go through `/skill:test` only; no ad-hoc `vitest`, and single-file runs are not a sanctioned reproduction channel (per AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R).
- **Blast radius:** the file has ~35 `boot*` helpers across 34 `describe` blocks and ~300 tests. Seeding changes the initial state of every suite in the file, so each affected suite must be re-verified; if a suite depended on unseeded variety, adjust that suite (with a comment) rather than leaving it flaky.
- **Do not weaken the assertions** to "at least one" just to go green — they must still catch a real double phase advance or a lost spawn.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is out of scope (managed by the ship pipeline).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — boot helpers (`bootPlay` `:654`, `bootPlayAtBoss` `:669`, `bootPlayWithAsteroid` `:684`), `bootSceneWithLevels` `:547`, `bootWithHordeWave` `:6261`, and the two assertions (`:1107`, `:2028`). Needs a shared seeded-boot helper plus loop-stop wiring.
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — deterministic boot that resumes the live loop; needs reading (not changing) to confirm loop-stop semantics.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `setRunSeed` `:5798`, `setRng` `:5781`, `_initRunSeed` `:5908`, `getAliveCount` `:5241`; read-only, existing seams.
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` / `createSeededRng()`; read-only.
- `src/test/powerUpTestFixtures.ts` — `createSeededRng` re-export used by the existing `FIXED_RNG` fixture.

## Related work

- AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R — same file, asteroid heading flake; fixed by seeding `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` and stopping the loop (completed).
- AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU — Robotron horde kill flake; fixed by seeding + isolating the kill (completed).
- AH-0MVF6VZG9000AN6E — per-describe boot reuse in heavy suites (completed).
- AH-0MVF6XQIC005RY3P — deterministic boot harness (fixed-delta boot, loop stop/resume).
- AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — where the two failures were discovered.
- AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3, AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ — the parent ACs of the two failing assertions.
- AH-0MV5L6BVN005DP4I — hold-full mineral pause that can freeze `tick()`; AH-0MURBER4L00821RR — `finishSpawnAnimations` seam.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** neither failure is a genuine gameplay regression (both passed on adjacent gates; the same code paths have dedicated deterministic suites). If the reproduced seed shows a real defect, raise it as a separate blocking item.
- **Risk (latent order-dependence):** seeding every suite may expose existing dependence on random layouts; treat each exposure as a found bug, not as a reason to leave the helper unseeded.
- **Risk (diff size):** seeding 35 helpers could balloon the diff; keep it to one shared helper plus one-line call-site changes.
- **Risk (scope creep):** production RNG behaviour must not change; any temptation to add a new production seam is out of scope.
- **Risk (verification cost):** the file has a 120 s per-test ceiling and 300 tests; use `/skill:test --scope changed` for the three-run loop and let the `dev`-push gate cover the full suite.
- **Scope-creep guard:** a general "no unseeded boot helper anywhere in the repo" guard test is a useful follow-up, not part of this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Answers recorded 2026-11-01 from the producer via interactive reply (all three recommendations accepted).

- **Q1 — Scope of seeding:** AC1 says *every* `boot*` helper (~35 across 34 `describe` blocks) must inject a seed. Options: (a) seed all helpers file-wide via one shared helper and re-verify each suite; (b) seed only the helpers used by the two flaky suites first, then extend file-wide in the same item; (c) seed only the two flaky suites and file the rest as a follow-up item.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the unseeded helpers are the latent flake source the item exists to remove, and a single shared helper keeps the diff small.
  **Answer (producer):** (a) as recommended. Source: interactive reply. Research: enumerated the helpers and `describe` blocks in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`; the existing seeded patterns are `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` (`setRng` + `game.loop.stop()`) and `bootWithHordeWave()` (`setRunSeed` before `scene.restart()`).
- **Q2 — Live rAF loop:** the item's "Likely cause" names only the unseeded RNG, but `bootPlay()`/`bootPlayAtBoss()` also leave the harness's resumed live loop running, which seeding cannot fix and which matches the "only under full-suite parallel load" signature. May AC1 be widened to cover stopping the live loop as well (as `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` already does)?
  **Recommended:** yes — deterministic boot must mean both a fixed seed and no wall-clock frame while the test asserts.
  **Answer (producer):** yes. Source: interactive reply. Research: `src/test/gameHarness.ts` stops the loop for its fixed-delta boot and then resumes it; `bootPlayWithAsteroid()` already stops it per test.
- **Q3 — Verification channel:** AC2 asks for "3 consecutive full-suite runs of the file", but repo policy forbids ad-hoc `vitest` and treats single-file runs as an unsanctioned reproduction channel. Should the evidence be three consecutive `/skill:test --scope changed` runs that include the file, plus the `dev`-push full-suite gate?
  **Recommended:** yes — that is the sanctioned channel and it also covers the full-suite requirement.
  **Answer (producer):** yes. Source: interactive reply. Research: `AGENTS.md` test-execution policy; AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R explicitly rejects single-file runs as a reproduction channel.
**Research note (no question asked):** AC1's reproduction-before-fix requirement is not an invented constraint — it is the precedent set in this file by AH-0MVG23LT7000CG4R and AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU, both of which rejected a green re-run as evidence. Source: those work items' descriptions.
